content.text: To confirm:
1) the issue is that when creating a container or binary resource using the Web UI the baseUrl is set incorrectly
2) this issue is with Fcrepo or fcrepo-message-consumer
Because the IndexerGroup messages in the provided logs are from fcrepo-message-consumer. (see
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-message-consumer/blob/master/fcrepo-message-consumer-core/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/indexer/IndexerGroup.java)
Also my understanding was that the baseUrl was the application base, everything after that is an id to some resource.
So in
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/mommy/kissing/santa_claus
http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest
is always the baseUrl
while
/mommy
/mommy/kissing
/mommy/kissing/santa_claus
are all ids depending on the resource you are acting on.
I feel like I may have misunderstood the issue?
, thoughts on the above?
Hello, original big reporter here.

Question 2: As far as I remember, the result of this bug causes an error in fcrepo-message-consumer, causing resources to not be indexed by the RDF indexer and likely the full text indexer, but I didn't get that far. This might be a bug in fcrepo-message-consumer or fcrepo.

Question 1: Yes, the baseUrl for the resource is set incorrectly when you create a resource using the WebUI... through a proxy. This might happen in a port-forwarding scenario, or when one is using a proxy server.
More details:  I was creating a virtual machine in Virtualbox. That virtual machine's fcrepo was available to the host at
http://localhost:38080
. Virtualbox would take any requests to that port on the host machine and forward them to port 8080 on the guest machine.
To reproduce:
Create a virtual machine in Virtualbox with port forwarding from a host port (like 38080) to the Fcrepo port (default is 8080, I think).
Install Fcrepo on the guest.
Install the RDF indexer and fcrepo-message-consumer.
Access the WebUI through the forwarded port.
Add a resource in the WebUI.
If the bug is reproducible in the latest version of Fcrepo: The indexer will not have statements for the newly created resource.

I think creating a resource in the WebUI set the baseURL of the resource to localhost:38080 (what's in the address bar) and not the baseURL of the server (localhost:8080). This causes the error in fcrepo-message-consumer.
It also means, depending on how you 'got to' the REST API, different resources would have different baseURLs. (localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest vs mydomain.net/fcrepo/rest) That's just speculation, though.
Let me know if you need any help. Thanks for looking at this.

Another quick comment: my interim fix for this issue was to create a resource on the guest machine locally using curl before making any resources in the WebUI through the forwarded port. If you only interact with the Fcrepo on the guest through the forwarded port on the host, you should be able to reproduce the issue.
Weirdly, creating even one resource on the guest locally fixes the issue. Maybe that 'sets' the baseURL for resources created in the future?
Looking at the source, it's weird that the baseURL sent to the message-consumer isn't always localhost:8080, since it's set by getBaseUri() on the injected UriInfo object.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/ceacc9832890906c8dee8f4533f5b33679d9b875/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/FedoraBaseResource.java#L83
So why did the indexer see the incorrect baseURL?
DEBUG 23:06:05.296 (IndexerGroup) Discovered baseURL:
http://localhost:38080/fcrepo/rest/
in message.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-message-consumer/issues/65
Have you tried to reproduce this on the most recent fcrepo4-vagrant?
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-vagrant
No, I'll try that now.
The error is reproducible in the latest fcrepo4-vagrant, if you change the host ports to something other than the defaults.
Pretty obvious why the ConnectException is thrown. localhost:38080 doesn't make sense in the guest. Seems it's not a problem with fcrepo-message-consumer, but with fcrepo.
git clone https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo4-vagrant.git
cd fcrepo4-vagrant
Changes to Vagrantfile:
config.vm.network :forwarded_port, guest: 8080, host: 38080
config.vm.network :forwarded_port, guest: 3030, host: 33030
dos2unix * # Grumble, only required on Windows hosts.
vagrant up
Coffee break
Visited
http://localhost:38080/fcrepo/rest/
and created a resource with identifier 'test'.
Run this in the WebUI at
http://localhost:38080/fcrepo/rest/test:
Then add a title:
Visited this url in the host, with no results:
http://localhost:33030/test/query?query=SELECT+%3Fs+%3Fp+%3Fo+WHERE+%7B%0D%0A%3Fs+%3Fp+%3Fo.%0D%0A%7D%0D%0A%0D%0A&output=xml&stylesheet=%2Fxml-to-html.xsl
I then added a dc:creator to the test resource, here's the tail of the log:

INFO 19:27:11.534 (FedoraLdp) PATCH for 'test'
DEBUG 19:27:11.579 (IndexerGroup) Received message: ID:fedora4-37720-1429038664816-3:1:1:1:8
DEBUG 19:27:11.580 (IndexerGroup) Discovered id: /test in message.
DEBUG 19:27:11.581 (IndexerGroup) Discovered event type: http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#PROPERTY_ADDED,http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#PROPERTY_CHANGED in message.
DEBUG 19:27:11.581 (IndexerGroup) Discovered baseURL: http://localhost:38080/fcrepo/rest in message.
DEBUG 19:27:11.581 (IndexerGroup) Discovered properties: http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#lastModified,http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#lastModifiedBy,http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/creator in message.
DEBUG 19:27:11.582 (IndexerGroup) It is false that this is a removal operation.
WARN 19:27:11.584 (DefaultMessageListenerContainer) Execution of JMS message listener failed, and no ErrorHandler has been set.
java.lang.RuntimeException: java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused at com.google.common.base.Throwables.propagate(Throwables.java:160) ~[guava-18.0.jar:na]
        at org.fcrepo.indexer.RdfRetriever.get(RdfRetriever.java:107) ~[fcrepo-message-consumer-core-4.1.1.jar:na]
        at org.fcrepo.indexer.RdfRetriever.get(RdfRetriever.java:51) ~[fcrepo-message-consumer-core-4.1.1.jar:na]
        at com.google.common.base.Suppliers$MemoizingSupplier.get(Suppliers.java:125) ~[guava-18.0.jar:na]
        at org.fcrepo.indexer.IndexerGroup.index(IndexerGroup.java:284) ~[fcrepo-message-consumer-core-4.1.1.jar:na]
        at org.fcrepo.indexer.IndexerGroup.onMessage(IndexerGroup.java:260) ~[fcrepo-message-consumer-core-4.1.1.jar:na]
...
Ok, I see the problem.

When coming through a proxy the resource is set with the outside port number (ie. 38080), but fcrepo-message-consumer uses the information from the JMS message to connect to fcrepo and get the resource.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-message-consumer/blob/3f5f08f374b7b354021f0272a1e3266cf423e3ff/fcrepo-message-consumer-core/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/indexer/IndexerGroup.java#L248
and
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-message-consumer/blob/3f5f08f374b7b354021f0272a1e3266cf423e3ff/fcrepo-message-consumer-core/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/indexer/IndexerGroup.java#L260
Internal to the VM, there is nothing at 38080, so it fails.
Not sure if this is expected behaviour or if fcrepo should generate all JMS messages using the server defined baseUrl?
I tested this using the latest fedora4_vm and it is reproducible.
However I got the same error when PUTting a new resource using Curl from the host side too. So it is definitely not the Web UI it is about how the baseUrl is set for the JMS message.
Not sure if you want to change this as if your JMS consumer was also outside the VM, then this is desirable functionality.
We get the baseURL from the userdata of the jcrEvent.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/43baef2b15829164584a33a5e13b2fa22d9f4d5b/fcrepo-jms/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/jms/headers/DefaultMessageFactory.java#L89
That's set here, from uriInfo.getBaseUri(), I think:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/ceacc9832890906c8dee8f4533f5b33679d9b875/fcrepo-http-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/api/FedoraBaseResource.java#L83
getBaseUri() should get the baseURI of the application, not the request. I haven't figured that out.
I may be in over my head, but I think it is in the HttpResourceConverter.
The
doBackward
refers to a
toDomain(doBackwardsPathOnly(resource))
which reverses the path and then builds a full URI for it.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-http-commons/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/http/commons/api/rdf/HttpResourceConverter.java#L159-L183
I don't know much about JAX-RS but I am guessing it is still working with the session that is creating that node, and it passed it as
localhost:38080
The HttpResourceConverter uses a translator initialized in
FedoraBaseResource
, that is initialized using the FedoraLdp.class.
That uses a javax.ws.rs.core.UriInfo in
AbstractResource
, which from documentation allows you to rebuild the Uri for a request without having it hard-coded. So the URI is based on the URI the request was sent to.
Probably because the VM doesn't touch the traffic it just re-directs it, hence the baseUri is built using the external facing port instead of the correct internal one.
Ok
probably need a decision from a higher power here.

Best I can think we could compare the URI built from the request to the server configuration and if they are different send two JMS messages (or maybe add an alternate address to the first message). \
That would allow internal consumers and external consumers to both work with one and fail with one.
But this is still a question of whether it is operating as designed?
Okay, further investigation reveals a little more.
This issue and Kevin's fix was due to the
this commit
with the addition of setBaseUrl to DefaultMessageFactory.
It was then removed 16 days ago (
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/1227c6107ac929fcb94d44ae0ae43f37fc9cf042)

Building with the 4.1.2-SNAPSHOT each request has a baseUrl built off of the request Url. So if I request from outside the VM the JMS message get the baseUrl of localhost:38080, if I request from inside it uses localhost:8080 and so on.
This is more of an expected behaviour (IMHO).
As
authored both of these commits I wonder if he could share some of the back story. Also he has done alot of work in here and might have some thoughts based on experience?

Specifically, why the baseUrl is now being set for each request instead of using either a) the baseUrl coming from the first request (which looked like their might be a memory leak) or b) using the container address instead (which I'm not sure if or how you might do that).

: the initial approach was setting the baseURL only once, to avoid problems with ObservationManager opening too many threads.  That bug was fixed, and a new requirement was added (tracking the userAgent which would vary between requests).  So we switched to setting the baseURL and userAgent with each request, and that seems to solve the other problem too.
: Is the issue identified in this ticket resolved as of 16 days ago?
If you're going to make the assumption that all clients (users, applications, indexers) will access the repository using the same address, that should be indicated in the setup documentation.

IMHO, an Indexer shouldn't ignore messages produced by a client that happens to use port forwarding or a proxy or an altered hosts file. The repository doesn't ignore those clients, so you'll get inconsistent data.
This issue could be closed as 'Won't Fix'.
I agree with Kevin that an assumption has been made when dealing with Fedora instances behind a NAT firewall. So I'd say no, it's not resolved by that commit.
It makes sense that the UriBuilder uses the request to generate the URLs it sends back, but for JMS messages it becomes more complicated.
I think I mentioned this before, but I feel we can either:
a) leave it as is and document this behaviour.
b) determine the web-app container server name and port and add those to the JMS Message as alternate baseUrls. This requires a change to the fcrepo-message-consumer, possibly fcrepo-camel?
c) some hybrid version, where you configure your Fedora instance if you are behind a NAT firewall and your JMS message consumer are as well.

I think a variant of c would be to have a system property (e.g. fcrepo.jms.baseUrl) that would override the default behavior and be used instead of getting the baseURL from the request.  If you are running your repository behind a proxy and want the message-consumer to use a different URL than what outside clients are using, then you'd set that property.
, sounds like a reasonable approach.
, are you available to implement it?
If this sounds acceptable to
, I can give it a go.
Could someone point to a previous example of using a system property. So I have a quasi-best practice to follow?
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-impl/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/impl/spring/DefaultPropertiesLoader.java#L86-L100
PR -
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/774
This looks good,
. Thanks.
Would you also please document the configuration of this feature as a new line item here:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Application+Configuration#ApplicationConfiguration-configelements
PR has been squashed and merged into the master branch with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/8779cf0581cbd4f7fb07e741bf7a8ac27af1b68d
Pending response to documentation comment above.
Added documentation. Could use a second look as I'm not sure I was clear (or perhaps too clear) that you can specify a host/port or full url.
Or if that level of documentation is just making murky that which would otherwise be clear.
Looks good. Thanks,
See:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/issues/677
